title.purpose: Page titles on the KG bar and state pages.

body.purpose: Evidence sentences and relation lines at 1.7 line-height inside the 56rem article.

mono.purpose: Identifiers, versions, counts; rendered on recessed chips with hairline borders.

motion.name: re-ink
motion.purpose: The only hover motion: chips, pills, and rows recolor border/text to teal; nothing lifts or translates.

motion.name: theme-flip
motion.purpose: Dark/light switch is immediate, no cross-fade, to avoid flashing content.

narrative.overview:
The page is a sheet of cool paper on the bench: quiet, slightly bluish-white, with dark ink and exactly one accent pen in deep teal. Everything on it is evidence, laid out the way a careful lab record reads — the claim as a sentence, the facts beneath it, the versions along the margin. Nothing competes with the content for attention.

This is a scientific instrument, not a brand exercise: flat surfaces, hairline borders, no shadows, no gradients, no decorative imagery. Colour is evidence, not decoration — it appears only where the markup also says what it means in words. Legibility wins every tradeoff, including thematic ones. Light cool paper is the default; slate bench is its equal after dark, both carrying the same single teal accent at matched contrast.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, bordered, tonal: depth comes from three neutral steps and 1px hairlines, never shadows.
One accent: deep teal (sea-glass after dark) marks links, actions, and current state — nothing else.
Words first: colour never carries meaning alone; every coloured signal has a text or marker twin.
Prose-first evidence: facts render as citable sentences with inline links, not label-value grids.
One left rail: header brand, headline, and evidence share a single left edge at every width.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Deep teal is the only hue that marks action or currency. Semantic green/red/amber appear only on state and always paired with words or +/- markers. No other color enters the system.

rules.name: The Words-First Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the only signal. Every diff line carries a +/- marker and a visually-hidden added/removed/changed word; every state kicker is text.

rules.name: The Tint, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Soft states use color-mix tints of the accent over the page background — never solid fills of the semantic color.

rules.name: The Sentence Rule
rules.body: Facts about an edge are written as prose sentences with links inline, never as label-value pairs. The claim and its evidence sit at the same size so they read as one argument.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: Identifiers always render in mono, never in body face. A bare identifier in prose face is a defect.

rules.name: The Flat Bench Rule
rules.body: Shadows, glows, and drop filters are banned at every level. Depth is a tonal decision, never a cast shadow. Hover re-inks instead of lifting.

dos: Do pair every colour signal with words or markers (+/-, uppercase kickers, hidden screen-reader text).
Do write edge facts as citable prose sentences at body size, with identifiers in mono chips.
Do keep header, headline, and content on the one 64rem left rail; center only terminal state pages (34rem).
Do use teal tints (color-mix at 10-18%) for soft states and solid teal only for actions and the current version.
Do keep both themes at matched contrast: when a light-mode color fails in dark, redesign the treatment, never just darken the text.
donts: Don't add shadows, glows, gradients, or any cast depth — the bench is flat at rest and on hover.
Don't introduce hues beyond the teal accent, Registry Blue, and the three-color state trio.
Don't center article content or split the left rail; the page reads as one grid with one left edge.
Don't render identifiers, versions, or counts in the body face; mono with a recessed chip is the only correct treatment.
Don't use amber as text in dark mode, and don't strip the research-use banner to a footnote — it is a legal boundary and keeps banner treatment in both themes.
Don't nest badges inside pills or buttons; siblings in a flex row keep every chip's border intact.
